title: Allow bucket paths to specify _count within a bucket

timeline.message: Allow bucket paths to specify _count within a bucket
timeline.author: Benjamin Trent

timeline.body:
Users should be able to specify specific metrics/keys within a specific bucket key. 

An example is `agg["bucket_foo"]._count`. 

This change now allows that.

closes: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/76320

timeline.body: Let's leave these reasons as comments then?  It may not be immediately obvious why some of these are wrong.

Unrelated to this PR, but `AggregationExecutionException` is the wrong thing to throw here.  That's a 500 class error, but this is a user error that should not be retried, which is what 400 class is for.  I opened https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/86273 to try to not lose track of it.
These examples should probably also land in the user facing docs
timeline.diff_hunk:
@@ -50,6 +51,16 @@ * {@code agg1>agg2>agg3.avg} - where agg1 and agg2 are both single-bucket aggs and agg3 is a multi-value metrics agg (eg stats, * extended_stats, etc...). In this case, the order will be based on the avg value of {@code agg3}. * + *
  • + * {@code agg1["foo"]>agg2>agg3.avg} - where agg1 is multi-bucket, and the path expects a bucket "foo", + * agg2 are both single-bucket aggs and agg3 is a multi-value metrics agg + * (eg stats, extended_stats, etc...). + * In this case, the order will be based on the avg value of {@code agg3}. + *
    • + *
  • + * {@code agg1["foo"]._count} - where agg1 is multi-bucket, and the path expects a bucket "foo". + * This would extract the doc_count for that specific bucket. + *

timeline.body: That path parser is a house of cards, and we should rewrite the whole thing to be more sensible, but that's out of scope for this I think.

@@ -46,6 +46,15 @@ PATH                =  <AGG_NAME><MULTIBUCKET_KEY>? (<AGG_SEPARATOR>, <AGG_NAME>
 For example, the path `"my_bucket>my_stats.avg"` will path to the `avg` value in the `"my_stats"` metric, which is
 contained in the `"my_bucket"` bucket aggregation.
 
+Here are some more examples:
++
+--
+ * `multi_bucket["foo"]>single_bucket>multi_metric.avg` will go to the `avg` metric in the `"multi_metric"` agg under the
+    single bucket `"single_bucket"` within the `"foo"` bucket of the `"multi_bucket"` multi-bucket aggregation.
+ * `agg1["foo"]._count` will get the `_count` metric for the `"foo"` bucket in the
+    multi-bucket aggregation `"multi_bucket"`
+--
+
 Paths are relative from the position of the pipeline aggregation; they are not absolute paths, and the path cannot go back "up" the
 aggregation tree. For example, this derivative is embedded inside a date_histogram and refers to a "sibling"
 metric `"the_sum"`:
